Subject: Multiparametric MRI Prostate | Date: 22 January 2025 | Institution: Ziekenhuis Gelderse Vallei (Ede)

Clinical context involves a previously confirmed malignancy with a current prostate-specific antigen measurement of 68.0 ng/mL and a history of a positive biopsy. The gland occupies 58.83 mL of space. T2-weighted sequences reveal a sharply demarcated, hypointense mass spanning roughly 28 mm along its longest axis. This abnormality concentrates within the right peripheral zone, encroaching upon the apical sector. Diffusion-weighted imaging shows pronounced restriction with correspondingly low apparent diffusion coefficient values, while dynamic contrast-enhanced phases capture early, robust enhancement. Capsular integrity remains intact, with no seminal vesicle infiltration detected. The transition zone maintains a benign architecture lacking significant hyperplastic nodules. Pelvic nodal basins appear unremarkable, and bone marrow signal shows no metastatic foci.

IMPRESSION:
PI-RADS 5 lesion in the right peripheral zone, consistent with clinically significant prostate cancer.
Prostate volume: 58.83 mL.
PSA density: 1.156 ng/mL/mL.
csPCa predicted probability 0.8985173

previous_notes.text: During a consultation on 04 February 2024, the primary care physician recorded a prostate-specific antigen elevation to 32.7 ng/mL alongside mild lower urinary tract complaints. Following documentation of the established positive biopsy status, a specialist evaluation was scheduled and standard observation continued for the interval. The encounter concluded without necessity for immediate acute measures.
